messages:
maya: hi everyone, new hire here — trying to run runtime unit tests after building from source in the dev container and seeing a hang during GPU init in kv_cache_test. first week on the job, any tips? :wave:

maya: output:

maya: ```
$ ./bazel-bin/runtime/tests/kv_cache_test --gtest_filter=KVCache.*
[ RUN      ] KVCache.AppendSmoke
[...hangs here for ~2m...]
```

mika: welcome! does the hang look like a blocking NVML call? check strace or run `LD_DEBUG=libs` to see dlopen/resolve issues.

maya: strace shows futex waits inside nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex_v2 and ldd on libredwood_runtime.so reported libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found. nvidia-smi on host shows Driver 535.86 / CUDA 12.2.

tiago: that matches other new-hire issues — dev containers sometimes don't mount host driver libs. quick local workaround: mount host libs into the container (`-v /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`) or create a symlink to the vendor lib if present.

infra-bot: Created INF-510: "devcontainer: nvml hang during unit tests - missing driver libs" assigned to infra oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-510 :ticket:

olivia: if you want to iterate without infra, set env `NVML_INJECTION_DISABLED=1` before running tests — that skips NVML probes. note: some tests assume GPU present and will short-circuit, so verify behaviour. also grep for global singletons that call DeviceTracker in ctors.

maya: thanks — `NVML_INJECTION_DISABLED=1` lets the test run past init, confirms NVML was culprit. i'll open a tiny PR to make the test harness set that env in local runs and link the infra ticket. appreciate the help! :heart:
